title: 𒋳𒈠 𒀸𒊭𒀜
titleEn: Laws of Hammurabi — §153–169: crimes in the family, betrothal gifts, dowries and disinheritance (xxv 61 – xxviii 37)
part: Laws §153–169 · family crimes, betrothal gifts & disinheritance (Col. xxv 61 – xxviii 37)
draftNote: The § chips number the laws (Harper’s sectioning, still standard); long laws span several tap-units. Readings checked sign-by-sign against Harper’s 1904 edition.
source: Louvre stele, after R.F. Harper, The Code of Hammurabi, King of Babylon (Chicago, 1904): transliteration and autograph plates, List of Signs. Readings are Harper’s in modern subscript notation. Cuneiform in Old Babylonian monumental sign forms via the SantakkuM webfont by Sylvie Vanséveren (CC BY 4.0); pronunciation: conventional reconstructed Old Babylonian. Audio: a German synthetic voice reads the Akkadian word by word from these pronunciation rules (word stress after Huehnergard). It cannot hold a consonant long, so doubled consonants are heard single (šumma with one m), and the emphatics ṭ and q are heard as plain t and k. Fresh translations made directly from the Akkadian; Harper’s public-domain translation consulted for sense only.

about: Seventeen laws about the family under strain. A wife who has her husband killed for another man is put on a stake (§153); then four laws on sex inside the family, all stated without softening: a father and his daughter, who is driven from the city (§154); a father and the bride chosen for his son, who is drowned if he lies with her after his son has known her, but only fined if the son had not (§155–156); a son and his mother, both burned (§157); a son caught in the lap of his father’s chief wife is cast out of his father’s house (§158). Next come the gifts that pass at a betrothal: if the groom changes his mind he loses what he brought; if the bride’s father changes his, he pays it back double; and a rival who slandered the groom does not get the girl (§159–161). Then what happens to a dead wife’s dowry (§162–164), how brothers share their father’s estate when he has favoured one son or married off all but the youngest (§165–166), and when a man had children by two wives (§167). The last two laws let a father disown his son, but only after the judges have examined the case, and only for a second grave offence (§168–169). Harper’s transliteration writes the Sumerian signs for ‘child’, ‘woman’, ‘house’, ‘silver’ and ‘bride’ as Akkadian words, and each was read from the plate; the few doubtful spellings are marked in the notes.

sentences.i: If a man’s wife has had her husband killed on account of another man, they shall put that woman on a stake.
sentences.n: A new law, and its verb is a causative. mussa ušdīk is “she has had her husband killed”: mussa (written mu-za) is mut “husband of” + -ša “her”, the t and š merged into ss as in §141–152, and ušdīk is the Š-stem of dâkum “to kill”. The Š-stem is the causative, marked by the š before the root (u-š-dīk), so “kill” becomes “cause to be killed”; Harper’s glossary lists it as the third stem of dâkum. aššum zikārim šanîm is “on account of another male”, the words of §132: aššum “because of” takes the genitive. The penalty is zinništam šuāti ina gašīšim išakkanūši, “that woman they shall set on a stake”: gašīšum is a stake or pole (Harper: “stake, pole”), and to set a person on one is to impale her; the text says no more than the words. zinništam is the sign SAL alone, išakkanū the plural present of šakānum “to set”, -ši “her”.

sentences.i: If a man has had intercourse with his daughter, they shall drive that man out of the city.
sentences.n: Incest with a daughter, stated without softening. mārassu is “his daughter”: DUMU “child” and SAL “woman”, then ZU for -ssu; the t of mārat and the š of -šu merge into ss, the same assimilation as in mussa. iltamad is the perfect of lamādum “to learn, to know”, and in this code “to know” a person is to have sex with her or him (Harper’s glossary: “know carnally”); the same verb returns in §155–156. awīlam šuāti is “that man”. ālam “the city” is one sign, URU (Harper prints alam). ušeṣṣûšu is the Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”, present plural, + -šu “him”: “they shall make him go out”. Harper prints u-še-iz-zu-u-šu, writing ṣ as z; the signs are IṢ and ZU, and the doubled ṣṣ they spell is what marks the present (the preterite would be ušēṣû). The penalty is banishment.

sentences.i: If a man has chosen a bride for his son, and his son has had intercourse with her,
sentences.n: A law about three people: a father, his son, and the bride the father has arranged for the son. The first clause is awīlum … iḫīrma, “a man has chosen (a bride) …”: iḫīr is the preterite of ḫiārum “to choose” (Harper: “to betroth”; the verb behind ḫīrtum “wife”), here “has chosen (a bride)”, with -ma “and”. ana mārišu “for his son” is ana + the genitive. kallātam “bride” is a Sumerogram, É.GI₄.A: the sign for house, the sign GI₄ and the sign A, three signs in all and no ending written (Harper’s glossary gives the same logogram, E.GE.A, and his List of Signs shows kallâtu as these three signs; his transliteration adds the case ending, kal-lâtam). The plate shows this spelling twice, at XXV 74 and XXVI 4. māršu ilmassi is “his son has known her”: lamādum “to know” (see §154) in the preterite, with -ši “her”; the d of ilmad and the š of -ši merge into ss, and the sign ZI writes the ssi.

sentences.i: and he afterwards has lain in her lap and they have caught him, they shall bind that man and throw him into the water.
sentences.n: The father is caught. šū warkānumma is “he afterwards” (warkānum “afterwards” + -ma). ina sūniša ittatīlma iṣṣabtūšu, “he has lain in her lap and they have seized him”, is the clause of §130 word for word: sūnum “lap”, ittatīl the perfect of itūlum “to lie”, iṣṣabtūšu the perfect plural of ṣabātum “to seize” (the t of the perfect is taken into the ṣ) with -šu “him”. Then the formula of §129: ikassûšuma (kasûm “to bind” + -šu + -ma) and ana mê inaddûši, “into the water they shall throw (him)”; nadûm is “to throw”. UNCERTAIN: the last word ends in -ši, which elsewhere is “her”, though the man is the object; the plate shows the sign ši there, and I translate “him” as the sense requires. The verdict is drowning, stated as plainly as every other penalty.

sentences.i: If a man has chosen a bride for his son, and his son has not had intercourse with her, and he himself has lain in her lap,

The condition is complete here; the penalty, which is a fine and not death, follows in the next unit.

sentences.i: If a man, after his father’s death, has lain in his mother’s lap, they shall burn them both.
sentences.n: Incest with the mother. warki abišu is literally “after his father”; the sense “after his father’s death” comes from the context, and the next law uses the same words. ina sūn ummišu is “in the lap of his mother”: sūn is sūnum in the construct state (written zu-un), ummišu is ummum “mother” + -šu; ittatīl as in §155. The text says only “burn”, and so do I.

sentences.i: If a man, after his father’s death, is caught in the lap of his father’s chief wife (?), who has borne children, that man shall be cast out of his father’s house.
sentences.n: Not the man’s mother this time but another woman of the house. rabītišu is rabûm “great, senior” in the feminine + -šu “his”, literally “his senior one”; I read “his” as the father’s and the woman as the father’s principal wife (Harper: “chief wife”), UNCERTAIN, because the word itself says neither whose she is nor that she is a wife. ša mārī waldat is “who has borne children” (mārī, DUMU with the plural signs; waldat the stative “she has borne”). ittaṣbat “he was caught” is the N-stem perfect, the passive, as in §129. The penalty is lighter than in §157: innassaḫ is the N-stem of nasāḫum “to pull out, to uproot”, “he shall be uprooted”, here cast out of the family house (Harper: “cut off”); the same verb carries §168–169. bīt abim “his father’s house” is written bît a-ba, where Harper’s a-ba stands for the genitive abim; the spelling is Harper’s, UNCERTAIN.

sentences.i: If a man who has had a present brought to his father-in-law’s house, and has given the bride-price,
sentences.n: The first of three laws about betrothal gifts; the first is the groom’s change of mind. The long “if” is built on a ša-relative clause: awīlum ša … ušābilu … iddinu, “a man who had (a present) brought … gave”; ša “who” makes both verbs end in -u, the subjunctive. bīt emišu is “the house of his father-in-law” (emum “father-in-law”). biblam is biblum “what is brought, a present” (Harper), the gift sent with the betrothal, which is separate from the tirḫatum “bride-price”. ušābilu is the Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”, so “had carried”: the groom does not carry it himself. iddinu is nadānum “to give”.

sentences.n: Three laws on the dowry (šeriqtum) of a wife who dies. aššatam iḫuz is “he has taken a wife” (iḫuz, the preterite of aḫāzum “to take”; the code’s usual way to say “married”). mārī ūlissumma is “children she bore him, and” (-ma “and”): ūlissum is ūlid “she bore” + -šum “to him”, the d and š merged into ss, and the last syllable is one complex sign, which Harper reads zum; his List of Signs has no entry for it, so the identification is UNCERTAIN (the same sign stands at XXVII 77). mārī is DUMU with the plural signs. ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” is the code’s phrase for dying, as in §12.

sentences.i: If a man has given a field, an orchard and a house to the son he favours (?), and has written him a sealed document,
sentences.n: A father’s gift to one son. ana mārišu ša īnšu maḫru is “to his son, whose eye is maḫru”: īnšu is īnum “eye” + -šu, and maḫru is the adjective “first, foremost” or a stative of maḫārum “to face”; the idiom is read as “the son he favours” (Harper: “favorite son”), UNCERTAIN. The gift is three Sumerograms: eqlam is A.ŠÀ, kirâm is {giš}KIRI₆, bītam is É, “a field, an orchard and a house”. išruk “he has given (as a gift)” is šarākum; Harper prints the last sign as uq in his text and uk in his glossary, and the sign UG (his List no. 62) reads either. kunukkam išṭuršum is “a sealed document he wrote for him”: kunukkum “sealed tablet”, šaṭārum “to write”, -šum “to him”; Harper’s kunukkam is written here ku-nu-kam, the last sign being the KAM sign (his List no. 157, kam/gam), as in the earlier laws. Two spots on the plate are UNCERTAIN: the ṭur of išṭuršum is drawn as a diamond with an inner triangle, not as the box-and-wedges DUMU sign (compare Harper’s List no. 53, dur), so the TUR glyph shown is only the nearest sign in the glossary; and at XXVII 34 a small extra sign stands between DUMU and ŠU that Harper’s mâri-šu does not record (a sign, or a flaw in the stone).

sentences.i: If he has committed a grave offence a second time, the father shall cast his son out of sonship.
sentences.n: Only on the second offence may the father disown him. adi šinīšu is “up to his second” = “a second time” (adi “up to”, šinā “two”, -šu; Harper’s glossary lists šinīšu), like adi 10-šu “tenfold” in §8. inassaḫ is “he shall uproot”, now without ul “not”: the same sentence as §168, made positive. With it the stele leaves the family of sons and fathers; §170 begins with a man’s children by a wife and by a slave-woman.

glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam · aššātim (aš-ša-tim) “wives”, the plural (aššātim iḫuz “he has taken wives”; the signs could also spell the singular aššatim)
glossary.aššum: because (of); concerning · because; with a clause, also “so that”, giving purpose or reason (aššum … lā ṣabātiša, UNCERTAIN in grammar)
glossary.aḫāzum: to take, grasp; Š-stem šūḫuzum “to make take hold” · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) preterite, iḫuzma “he took, and”; present iḫḫaz (i-iḫ-ḫa-az) “he shall take”, which also serves as a permission, “he may take”; iḫḫazu (i-iḫ-ḫa-zu, with the subjunctive -u) “(before) he takes”; infinitive aḫāzim (a-ḫa-zi-im), taking its object in the genitive; taḫḫazanni (2nd person, with -anni “me”) · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) “he has taken (a wife)”, iḫuzma, itaḫazma (i-ta-ḫa-az-ma, perfect + -ma) “he has taken, and”; present iḫḫaz “he shall take”, aḫḫaz “I shall take” (a-ḫa-az, the doubling not written), taḫḫaz “you shall take”; iḫzu (iḫ-zu) with the relative -u: ša aššatam lā iḫzu “who has not taken a wife”; iḫḫazzi (i-iḫ-ḫa-az-zi) “he shall take her” (-ši, z and š merged)
glossary.aḫāzum-Š: Š-stem of aḫāzum “to take”: to make take, have (a man) take (a wife): ušaḫḫazūšu (u-ša-aḫ-ḫa-zu-šu) “they shall have him take (a wife)” (present plural + -šu “him”)
glossary.biblum: what is brought, a present (Harper); the gift sent at a betrothal, separate from the tirḫatum “bride-price”: biblam (bi-ib-lam) “a present” (accusative)
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading)
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone
glossary.dâkum-Š: Š-stem of dâkum “to kill” (the causative; Harper’s third stem): to have (someone) killed: ušdīk (uš-di-ik) “she has had (her husband) killed”
glossary.eliāt: beyond, over and above (before a genitive): eliāt zittišu (e-li-a-at) “over and above his share”
glossary.elēnumma: in addition, over and above, besides; used for a surcharge
glossary.emum: father-in-law (the bride’s father): emišu (e-mi-šu) “of his father-in-law”, bīt emišu “the house of his father-in-law”; emim (e-mi-im) genitive; emušu (e-mu-šu) “his father-in-law” as subject
glossary.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”)
glossary.gašīšum: stake, pole (Harper): ina gašīšim (ga-ši-ši-im) “on a stake”; to set a person on one is to impale
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
glossary.itūlum: to lie down, lie with: ittatīlma “he has lain, and” (perfect, in the -ma chain, §130); infinitive itūlim, utūlim “lying” (Harper prints both i-tu-lim and u-tu-lim), in “caught lying with another male”
glossary.ištu: after, since; from; as a conjunction, “after, once”: ištu … īteliānim “after … have come up”
glossary.ištēn: one: šattam ištiatma “one year only” · ištiššu (iš-ti-iš-šu) “for the first time” (ištēn + -šu)
glossary.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence”
glossary.kallatum: bride (for a son), written with the Sumerogram É.GI₄.A, three signs and no ending written (Harper’s transliteration adds the ending, kal-lâtam): kallātam “a bride”
glossary.karāṣum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of karāṣum, Harper’s “to slander”: uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (perfect + -šu “him”, ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU); the verb is rare and the form is not secure, the sense is Harper’s
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price”
glossary.kasûm: to bind, tie up (probable, not certain; Harper’s i-ka-zu has the ZU sign, read su): ikassûšunūtima “they shall bind them” (-šunūti “them”, -ma “and”) · ikassûšuma (i-ka-zu-šu-ma) “they shall bind him, and” (-šu “him”, -ma “and”)
glossary.kilallān: both (of two): kilallašunu (ki-la-la-šu-nu) “both of them”, with -šunu “their, of them” · kilallīšunu (ki-la-li-šu-nu) “both of them” (Harper writes li here, la elsewhere)
glossary.kirûm: orchard, garden (written {giš}SAR, the KIRI₆ sign): kirāšu “his orchard”
glossary.lamādum: to learn, to know; of a person, to know carnally (Harper): iltamad (il-ta-ma-ad, perfect) “he has known (his daughter)”; ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her” (preterite ilmad + -ši “her”, d + š said ss, spelled with the sign ZI); ilmassima (il-ma-zi-ma) “has known her, and”
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and”
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share”
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.makkūrum: property, assets — written with the Sumerogram Harper reads ŠA.GA (modern NÍG.GA)
glossary.mala: as many as, as much as (introducing a relative clause): mala ina kirîm ibbaššû “as many as are in the orchard”
glossary.manûm: mina — weight of silver, 60 shekels (about 500 g): 1 mana kaspim · spelled in syllables, ma-na, at §59: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver”
glossary.maḫrûm: first, former, previous: maḫrītim in šattim maḫrītim “in the previous year” · maḫru (maḫ-ru) “first, foremost” (an adjective or a stative of maḫārum): ša īnšu maḫru, read “the son he favours” (UNCERTAIN)
glossary.mitḫāriš: equally, in equal parts, on an equal footing
glossary.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”)
glossary.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter”
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers”
glossary.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him”
glossary.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present)
glossary.nasāḫum-N: N-stem of nasāḫum, the passive: to be uprooted, cast out (of a family house): innassaḫ (in-na-az-za-aḫ) “he shall be cast out”
glossary.palāsum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of palāsum, Harper’s “to look with longing”: uptallisma (up-ta-al-li-is-ma) “he has looked longingly (at another woman), and” (perfect + -ma); the verb is rare
glossary.parāsum: to decide, cut off: iprus · iparrasūma (i-par-ra-su-ma) “they shall investigate, and” (present plural + -ma; Harper: “to decide, to investigate, to inquire into”)
glossary.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”) · idioms: panam šakānum “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind; panīšu wabālum “to carry his face” = to overlook an offence (UNCERTAIN)
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma
glossary.qalûm: to burn (Harper qalû): iqallû(ši) “they shall burn (her)” · iqallûšunūti (i-qal-lu-u-šu-nu-ti) “they shall burn them” (present plural + -šunūti “them”)
glossary.qīštum: gift: qīšti šarrum ana rēdîm iddinu “the gift the king gave the soldier”
glossary.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN
glossary.ragāmum: to claim, to call out a claim: irgumu (ir-gu-mu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he claimed” · iraggum (i-ra-ag-gu-um) “he shall claim” (present with the ventive -m): ul iraggum “he shall not claim”
glossary.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired”
glossary.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN
glossary.sūnum: lap, bosom: sūniša “her lap” (written zu-ni-ša); ina sūniša ittatīl “he lay in her lap” · sūn (zu-un) construct, “the lap of”: ina sūn ummišu “in the lap of his mother”
glossary.tabālum: to take away, carry off: itabbal · tabal “take!” (imperative) · itbal (it-ba-al, preterite) “he took away” · itbalam (it-ba-lam, preterite + the ventive -am) “he has brought (it)”, the form that serves for “bring on”: ana abišu itbalam “he has brought (it) to his father”
glossary.tirḫatum: bride-price, the marriage payment (understood as the groom’s gift): tirḫatum “the bride-price”, tirḫatiša “her bride-price” · tirḫatam, tirḫatim (tir-ḫa-tam, tir-ḫa-tim) “the bride-price”, the groom’s payment to the father-in-law, which is returned (utâr, uttēršum) or deducted from the dowry (iḫarraṣma)
glossary.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr
glossary.ummum: mother: ana ummišu “to his mother”, ummašu urabbāšu “his mother shall raise him” · ummātim (um-ma-tim) plural “mothers”: ana ummātim “by mothers”; ummātišunu “their mothers”
glossary.wabālum: to bring, carry: itbalam “he brought”, lū ublam “let me bring” · ublū (preterite, plural, in a ša-clause) “(the water) carried off” · ublam “he has brought”; lā ublam “he has not brought (on himself)”; ublu (ub-lu) “(which) he brought” (the relative -u); ubbalū (ub-ba-lu) “they shall carry”: panīšu ubbalū “they shall carry his face” = overlook it (UNCERTAIN idiom)
glossary.wabālum-N: N-stem of wabālum “to carry”, the passive (Harper: passive, IV 1, of “to bring”): ibbablušum (ib-ba-ab-lu-šum) “(what) was brought to him” (preterite + the subjunctive -u of a ša-clause + -šum “to him”)
glossary.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off” · ušābilšu (u-ša-bil-šu, preterite) “he had (him) carry”; šūbulu (šu-bu-lu, Š stative šūbul with the subjunctive -u) “(what) has been sent”, šūbulūma (šu-bu-lu-ma) “has been sent, and”; the stative reading is from the form and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN · ušābil (u-ša-bi-il) “he has had (a present) brought” (preterite, without -u where there is no ša); ušābilu (u-ša-bi-lu) “who had (a present) brought” (with the relative -u)
glossary.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u) · ūlissum (u-li-zum) “she bore him” (ūlid + -šum, d and š said ss; the last sign is one complex sign, its identification UNCERTAIN) · waldat (wa-al-da-at) “she has borne” (stative): ša mārī waldat “who has borne children”
glossary.warka: afterwards, later · as a conjunction before a clause, “after”: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context
glossary.warki: after, behind: warkišu “after him, in his absence”
glossary.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city”
glossary.zikārum: male, man as a sex (opposed to a woman): zikaram, zikārim “a male”
glossary.zinništum: woman (written with the single sign SAL, ŠAL in Harper): zinništam, zinništim, zinništum
glossary.zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA): zittašu, zittišu “his share” · zittam (ṣi-it-tam, the ZI sign read ṣi by Harper and zi here, as in ezēbim) “a share”: zittam kīma aplim ištēn “a share like one heir’s”
glossary.zâzum: to divide, share: izuzzū “they shall divide”
glossary.ālum: city (URU): ālum u rabiānum “the city and the mayor”
glossary.īnum: eye: īnšu … iššīma “he lifted his eye (to it)” — he coveted it · ša īnšu maḫru (i-in-šu) “whose eye is first” = the son he favours (UNCERTAIN idiom)
glossary.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind
glossary.šalāmum-D: D-stem of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make good, restore (Harper: “to restore”): ušallamma (u-ša-lam-ma) “he shall make good, and”
glossary.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive
glossary.šanûm-Š: UNCERTAIN: šanûm “to repeat, do a second time”, so perhaps “to double”; uštašannâ (uš-ta-ša-an-na-ma, with -ma “and”) is a Š-stem perfect (ušta- is the perfect prefix) and is read as “he shall double (it)”, but the exact stem and the form are not secure; the sense follows the penalty of the law · on the stele (§101): uštašannâma (uš-ta-ša-na-ma, with -ma “and”) “he shall double (it)”, which Harper’s glossary lists as a Š-stem perfect of šanû “to duplicate, to double”; the form is as Harper has it and the exact stem is not secure
glossary.šaqālum: to weigh out (silver = to pay): išqulu · išaqqal (present) “he shall weigh out”
glossary.šarākum: to give away, hand over: ištarak · išruk (iš-ru-uq) “he has given (as a gift)” (the last sign UG, read uq or uk)
glossary.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document”
glossary.šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138 · šeriqtiša (še-ri-iq-ti-ša) “her dowry”, šeriqti (še-ri-iq-ti, construct) “the dowry of”: šeriqtaša ša mārīšama “her dowry is her children’s alone”; šeriqtaša ša bīt abiša-ma “her dowry is her father’s house’s alone”
glossary.šinā: two (šinā); šinīšu (ši-ni-šu) “his second (time)”: adi šinīšu “up to his second time”, i.e. a second time
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šunūti: them (masculine plural, accusative): ṣarrūtim šunūti “those criminals” · as the verbal suffix -šunūti “them”: iqallûšunūti “they shall burn them”
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
glossary.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
glossary.ḫarāṣum: to cut off, deduct (Harper: “to deduct”): iḫarraṣma (i-ḫar-ra-aṣ-ma) “he shall deduct, and” (present + -ma)
glossary.ḫiārum: to choose; to betroth (Harper; the verb behind ḫīrtum “wife”): iḫīrma (i-ḫi-ir-ma) “he has chosen (a bride), and” (preterite + -ma)
glossary.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize” · iṣbassuma (iṣ-ba-zu-ma, ZU for -ssu) “it seized him, and” (preterite iṣbat + -šu + -ma), of a debt seizing a man · iṣṣabtūšu (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tu-šu) “they seized him” (perfect, plural, with -šu “him”); iṣṣabat (iṣ-ṣa-ba-at) “he has seized (his wife)” (perfect) · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (perfect + -ši, t + š said ss); present plural iṣabbatū (i-ṣa-ba-tu) “they shall seize”; preterite with the subjunctive iṣbatu; infinitive with suffix ṣabātiša “seizing her”
glossary.ṣabātum-N: to be seized, caught (N-stem, passive of ṣabātum): iṣṣabit “she was caught” (preterite, in lā iṣṣabit); ittaṣbat “she was caught” (perfect)
glossary.ṣeḫrum: young; the child: mār awīlim ṣeḫram “the young son of a free man”
